items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: But they don’t know Michael Brecker’s got the technique to do that.

ctx.x: And if they stumble over it for a while, and sometimes if you let them stumble, now this is the part of jazz, this might be an important statement, this is the part of jazz that I think isn’t happening. They won’t let them try enough now, the schools are too lazy ‘cause they can go to the teachers and get jazz lessons and learn everything else, learn everything, the solo and all the technical aspects, all the embouchures, all the breathing, everything else is off. And they’re going to continue to do that, where…

Michael Brecker they say, “well man, I’ve arrived now.” I say all right, just remember you got Michael Brecker then. Just remember you got Coltrane. Just remember you got Charlie Parker when you get to that point. Your imitation of what they did. So that’s the thing.
